findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify where harvest_structured_into_bank obtains the marker value (e.g. preserve the existing bank entry's marker on overwrite, since the model never emits it) so re-harvest cannot drop an insufficient marker.
evidence: completion_banking.py:573 records = result.get('criteria') — harvest reads the model's structured output only
Plan: 'the marker is never a model-tool input' and new :544 rule 'not-found evidence records nothing'
Plan AC: 'Marker-carrying entries survive harvest_structured_into_bank round-trips' — but no source is named for a harvest-time marker given the model does not emit it
findings.finding: The marker is declared framework-set and 'never a model-tool input', and the new :544 rule tells the model to record NOTHING for not-found evidence — yet harvest_structured_into_bank reads only the model's structured output (result['criteria']) to upsert. The plan asserts 'markers survive harvest round-trips' and 'markers survive re-harvest' without specifying where the marker VALUE comes from on the harvest write path, since the model never emits it.
scenarios: A criterion banked as insufficient by the bounded fallback is later re-harvested from a successor's structured output that lacks the marker; harvest overwrites and the marker is lost (or the plan intends idempotent no-op overwrite — unclear)
findings.suggested_fix: State that harvest reads the incoming record's marker if present else preserves the prior bank entry's marker, and add an explicit round-trip test that a fallback-banked insufficient entry keeps its marker after a marker-less successor re-harvest.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `_findings_for_unmet` (completion_banking.py:750-774) to the Scope inventory and specify that it must branch on the `evidence_sufficient:false` marker to emit insufficient-evidence finding text (not the hard-coded 'criterion not met' high-severity finding) for `merge_finalizer_with_bank`'s marker-carrying records.
evidence: Plan: 'marker-carrying entries emit `met:false + evidence_sufficient:false` with an insufficient-evidence finding, not a bare unmet-criterion FAIL finding' — named only `assemble_deterministic_verdict :619-640` and `merge_finalizer_with_bank :705-714`.

Scope bullet enumerates completion_banking.py symbols: `upsert`, `record_criterion_verdict`, `harvest_structured_into_bank`, `both placeholder branches`, `merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamp (both branches)` — `_findings_for_unmet` is absent.
completion_banking.py:734-735: `merge_finalizer_with_bank` calls `_findings_for_unmet(records, result.get("findings"))` to build the FAIL findings list.
completion_banking.py:765-773: `_findings_for_unmet` emits `{"detail": "criterion not met (banked/unverified).", "severity": "high"}` for every unmet record with no branch on the marker.
findings.finding: For the `merge_finalizer_with_bank` rendering seam, the plan requires marker-carrying entries to emit an 'insufficient-evidence finding' rather than a 'bare unmet-criterion FAIL finding', but the per-criterion FAIL finding text for this path is NOT generated inside `merge_finalizer_with_bank` — it is produced by the separate helper `_findings_for_unmet` (completion_banking.py:750-774), which the plan's Scope and consumer-graph inventory never names. That helper hard-codes `detail="criterion not met (banked/unverified)."` at `severity:"high"` for every unmet record, so an insufficient (marker-carrying) entry still gets bare unmet-criterion finding text unless the helper is patched.
findings.location: Proposed fix → 'Banked-entry rendering (`assemble_deterministic_verdict` :619-640, `merge_finalizer_with_bank` :705-714)' and Scope → completion_banking.py bullet
scenarios: completion_banking.py `_findings_for_unmet` (:750-774): an insufficient (marker-carrying) criterion flowing through `merge_finalizer_with_bank` still receives the hard-coded 'criterion not met (banked/unverified).' high-severity finding, so the seam violates the acceptance criterion 'Both rendering seams emit ... an insufficient-evidence finding' despite the record itself carrying `evidence_sufficient:false`.
Test file: a per-seam/per-branch test for `merge_finalizer_with_bank` insufficient rendering would fail on finding text because the uninventoried helper was not patched.
findings.suggested_fix: In the completion_banking.py Scope bullet and the 'Banked-entry rendering' paragraph, name `_findings_for_unmet` alongside `merge_finalizer_with_bank`, and state that it selects insufficient-evidence detail/severity when a record carries `evidence_sufficient:false`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the severity and finding class/detail vocabulary the insufficient-evidence finding carries (e.g. keep high severity but distinct detail text), consistently across assemble_deterministic_verdict, merge_finalizer_with_bank, and the finalizer prompt.
evidence: Plan: 'marker-carrying entries emit met:false + evidence_sufficient:false with an insufficient-evidence finding, not a bare unmet-criterion FAIL finding'
completion_banking.py:637,:658 hard-code 'severity': 'high' for placeholder findings
finalizer prompt :26 'Include one high-severity finding for every criterion with met: false'
The plan never states the severity/class of the insufficient finding — an emitted-value vocabulary left undefined
findings.finding: The plan introduces an 'insufficient-evidence finding' emitted by both rendering seams and the finalizer prompt but never defines the SEVERITY (or finding class/detail vocabulary) it carries; the existing placeholder/unmet findings are hard-coded severity=high (completion_banking.py:637,:658) and the finalizer prompt mandates 'one high-severity finding' (finalizer md:26), so the executor must guess whether insufficient findings stay high or take a new class.
findings.location: Plan 'Full consumer graph' > Banked-entry rendering; completion_verifier_finalizer.md:23-28
scenarios: Executor writes the insufficient finding at 'high' severity, indistinguishable in severity from a genuine refutation; or invents a new severity inconsistently across the two seams

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the precedence when the finalizer's own judgment on a criterion conflicts with the bank's insufficient marker: re-stamp the marker ONLY when the finalizer did not itself refute the criterion (finalizer refutation wins over a bank insufficient marker), so a genuine refutation is never relabeled insufficient.
evidence: merge_finalizer_with_bank docstring (:691-692): 'preserving the finalizer's own judgments (including a cross-criterion downgrade of a banked met=true)' — the finalizer can change a verdict
Plan: 'the bank (not the model's structured output) is the source of truth for the marker ... the merge overwrites the finalizer's echo'

The bank carries the insufficient marker ONLY because the fallback banked it (no model refutation); if the finalizer independently refutes that same criterion, an unconditional bank re-stamp would mask the refutation as insufficient
findings.finding: The plan makes merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamp the per-criterion marker from the bank as 'the source of truth', but the finalizer retains independent cross-criterion refutation/downgrade authority; re-stamping a bank 'insufficient' marker over a criterion the finalizer genuinely REFUTED would relabel evidence-of-absence back to absence-of-evidence — the inverse of the bug.
findings.location: Proposed fix — Banked-entry rendering; merge_finalizer_with_bank (completion_banking.py:680-738, existing-record branch :700-704)
scenarios: Fallback banks criterion X as met=false+insufficient; the finalizer, seeing the full criteria set, positively refutes X; merge re-stamps insufficient from the bank and X is reported as 'insufficient evidence' rather than a genuine unmet-criterion FAIL finding.
findings.suggested_fix: In merge_finalizer_with_bank's existing-record branch, look up the bank entry and re-stamp evidence_sufficient:false only when the finalizer's echoed record did NOT supply its own refutation finding for that criterion; a finalizer that positively refutes overrides the bank's insufficient marker.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that not-found criteria reach the insufficient marker via TWO framework paths — the bounded fallback (>=3 evidence calls) AND the unbanked/exhausted placeholder branches (fewer evidence calls or never reached) — so the '<3 evidence calls, records nothing' case is covered.
evidence: completion_tool_policy.py:182: fallback fires only 'if target_id is not None and evidence_count >= policy.max_evidence_responses'
Plan: 'not-found evidence records nothing — the bounded fallback (completion_tool_policy.py:187) fires at the boundary and banks the marker'
For a not-found criterion the model examines with <3 evidence calls and then commits nothing to, the fallback never fires; coverage depends entirely on the unbanked placeholder branch
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'ALL absence-of-evidence flows through the framework's marker path' via the bounded fallback (completion_tool_policy.py:187), but the fallback only fires on the THIRD evidence tool call (evidence_count >= max_evidence_responses); a model that follows the new :544 rule and records nothing after FEWER than three evidence calls leaves the criterion unbanked and reliant on the unbanked/exhausted placeholder path, not the fallback. The plan does not make this dual routing explicit.
findings.location: Proposed fix — record_criterion_verdict :544 new rule; wrap_completion_evidence_policy (completion_tool_policy.py:182-188)
scenarios: Model makes one or two evidence calls on a hard-to-find criterion, finds nothing, records nothing per the new rule, and moves to the next id; the criterion is never banked and only the deterministic/finalizer placeholder (not the fallback) supplies its insufficient marker.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the concrete per-criterion input signal in the _run_finalizer payload that the finalizer reads to emit insufficient-evidence (vs refutation) text, and align the prompt rule to that signal.
evidence: finalizer prompt :24-25 'Missing, incomplete, contradictory, or truncated evidence is not enough and must be met: false' — no exhaustion/refutation distinction
Plan: 'banked insufficient entries echo as met:false with insufficient findings text; merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamps the marker from the bank (stamp = enforcement, prompt = text alignment)'
Plan says the re-stamp is authoritative, implying the prompt's echo need not be trusted — but the prompt rule still must tell the model what input to read
findings.finding: The tool-free finalizer keys only on the bank's per-criterion evidence REPORT text (the _run_finalizer payload) and cannot see the framework-set marker as a decision signal; the plan says _run_finalizer's payload 'carries the marker' and the prompt rule says 'banked insufficient entries echo as met:false with insufficient findings text', but it never specifies the concrete INPUT signal in the finalizer's payload that the model reads to distinguish an insufficient (exhausted) entry from a genuinely refuted one. The current prompt collapses missing/incomplete/contradictory/truncated all into met:false.
scenarios: Finalizer receives an exhausted entry, has no marker field to key on, and produces refutation-style finding text that the re-stamp then contradicts — text/marker mismatch
